title: Turkmenistan
subtitle: from Dashoguz to Ashgabat
standfirst: Photos from Turkmenistan at the end of July 2015. A transit visa let me travel on my own, but only through two cities: Dashoguz, near the Uzbek border, and Ashgabat.

cover.alt: Two white buildings with arched windows and flags on their roofs, cars crossing a junction in front, Ashgabat

stops.caption: Dashoguz, the first town over the border from Uzbekistan. From here the road runs south across the Karakum Desert to Ashgabat.

photos.alt: A gilded statue on a pedestal in front of a white colonnade and a tall flagpole, a child pushing a pram across the square
A tree-lined avenue with lit street lamps leading to a gold monument and a domed white building
A large white building outlined in gold lights, its centre shaped like an open book, a car and a cyclist on the road in front
A waiting room with metal bench seats and a row of computers along the wall, people seated with their backs to the camera
The white railway station in Dashoguz, a portrait of President Berdimuhamedow above the entrance under the gold letters of 'Wokzal'
A police officer and another man beside a blue roadside building in the desert, seen through a car windscreen
A corrugated-iron shelter on bare ground in the Karakum Desert, scrub and low dunes behind

stops.caption: Ashgabat, the capital, under the Kopet Dag. The herbs in the bazaar are labelled in Russian and Turkmen. From here, south over the mountains to Mashhad.

photos.alt: A bazaar stall of dried herbs, flowers and berries in wooden trays, handwritten labels in Russian and Turkmen, the seller behind
Traffic on a wide avenue in Ashgabat, white apartment blocks and the Kopet Dag mountains ahead, seen from a car
Turkmen newspapers on a glass table, each front page with a photograph of President Berdimuhamedow, beside a tourism magazine
A supermarket aisle in Ashgabat, staff restocking an open fridge of butter and cheese, a red crate in the middle
